title: Cancelling an armed gate drops focus to the page; Escape then closes the card
body:
## Summary
When an armed Gate is cancelled or confirmed, the focused button unmounts and focus falls to document.body; the next Escape leaves the card as well as the decision list, and Tab escapes both focus traps.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Gate.tsx:54` swaps the armed group and the idle button inside `AnimatePresence mode="wait"`; Cancel (`Gate.tsx:79`) and the confirm's `after` (`Gate.tsx:75`) set `armedOn` to null and nothing moves focus. The focused button is removed, so `document.activeElement` is the body for the exit fade and after it. `card/Decide.tsx` handles Escape and Tab in its pane's `onKeyDown`, which a keydown on the body never reaches; the kit's window rule (`examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/escape.ts:26`, MODAL_SELECTOR) sees an Escape from outside any modal and steps the level up, closing the card, which unmounts the decision list with it. Fixed means focus stays inside the pane on disarm: on a stable wrapper synchronously, then on the idle button when it mounts, or on the dialog heading when the row is now disabled. The kit's `useOverlayEscape` already states the rule this breaks: focus never goes to `document.body`.

## Flow
- L2 card -> Decide next step -> Record it (arms; confirm focused) -> Cancel
- focus is on the body; press Escape
- observed by reading the code: the window rule runs nav.up, the card and the decision list both close; one press left two things

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users who back out of a gated act lose their place and the dialog; measured by a DOM test asserting activeElement stays inside `.ln-decide` after Cancel and that one Escape closes only the list. Could break: focus landing on a disabled idle button (the row turned blocked) - the fix needs the heading fallback.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one Escape leaves one thing after a gate is backed out of
Before: by the code: after Cancel activeElement = body on 3 of 3 gates; Escape then closes 2 layers
After: predicted: focus inside the pane on 3 of 3, Escape closes 1 layer
Method: simulation - walked from Gate.tsx, Decide.tsx onKeyDown and escape.ts; the ledgerbox runner cannot load JSX and has no DOM, so no gate or probe was reachable this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Gate.tsx:54  <AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false}>
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Gate.tsx:79  <button ... data-kind="ghost" onClick={() => setArmedOn(null)}>Cancel
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/Decide.tsx:175  const onKeyDown = (event) => { overlay.onKeyDown(event); ... }  (on the pane, not the window)
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/escape.ts:26  MODAL_SELECTOR = '[role="dialog"],[role="alertdialog"],[aria-modal="true"]'  (body is in none)
instrument: a DOM test (happy-dom, as apps/desktop's *.dom.test.tsx) mounting Decide with a Gate: press Cancel, assert activeElement is inside .ln-decide; dispatch Escape, assert only the list closed

title: Refiling from the card leaves it in the lane the invoice left
body:
## Summary
After Refile on an open card, the card keeps the old lane's name and the way back leads into a lane that no longer holds the invoice.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Lanes.tsx:140` reads `lane = laneById(sheet, focus.group)` and `mark = markById(sheet, focus.item)`; `markById` searches every lane (`components/lanes/model/filters.ts:92`), so after `categorizeAction` and the refresh the card stays open on the moved invoice while `focus.group` is still the old area. The card's eyebrow (`Lanes.tsx:333`, `laneLabel={lane?.label ?? mark.category}`) and the crumb (`shell/Foot.tsx:107`) name the old area, and `nav.up` lands in an L1 whose cards do not include the invoice, so the lift has no node to fly back to. Fixed means the focus follows the mark: when `mark.category !== focus.group` at L2, re-point the nav to `openItem(mark.category, mark.id)` (or at least label from the mark's own lane).

## Flow
- L0 -> open Design -> open an invoice -> Decide next step -> File under: Retainers -> Refile
- the sheet refreshes; the card eyebrow and the crumb still say Design
- Escape -> L1 Design, which no longer contains the invoice; the card has no node to land on

## Expected impact
Anyone refiling from the card (the only person path to categorize) sees the wrong area named and loses the invoice on the way back. Measured by a probe on scratch books (refile, rebuild, laneById(focus.group) lacks the mark) and a browser check of the return. Could break: a re-point mid-L2 starts a level flight; it must not replay the lift.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card names and returns to the area the invoice is in
Before: probe on the seed: refile 1 invoice from its card; laneById(sheet, focus.group).marks contains it: false; label shown = old area
After: predicted: label = new area; nav.up lands in the lane holding it
Method: simulation - the probe half was taken (sheet side); the render and the nav re-point need a browser or a DOM test this round does not have
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a probe on scratch books (categorize from L2 focus, rebuild, compare focus.group to mark.category) plus a browser or DOM check that nav.up lands on the mark's lane

title: Send it is confirmed without the letter it sends on the decision surface
body:
## Summary
The Send it gate names the address and that it cannot be un-sent, but not the letter; the draft is in the card's evidence column, under the decision list's scrim.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/Decide.tsx` (send row): `reaches` is "Reaches <contact> at <email> by email. You cannot un-send it." and the gate's question "This reaches <email>. You cannot un-send it."; the body lives in `card/Evidence.tsx:130` ("Draft reminder, <tone>, not sent"), inside the card that `.ln-decide-layer` (style/level2/l2-the-card-3.css:155, z-index 70 over the card's 60) covers. hitl-approval golden path: "The human decides on the real thing. The decision surface shows the actual content, diff, or disclosed impact"; decision-records: what the decider was shown is part of the record. Since 9fc4636 the gate is armed on the letter's text, so what is approved is pinned - but the person is not shown it where they press. Fixed means the send row (or its armed question) carries the letter, or its subject and first lines with a way to read the rest, inside the decision list.

## Flow
- L2 card of an invoice with a draft -> Decide next step
- the send row shows the recipient and the irreversibility; the letter is under the scrim
- Send it -> Send it: the yes is to a letter the surface did not show

## Expected impact
The person sending a reminder (the one act that reaches a client) sees what they are sending at the moment they send it. Measured in a browser: the letter's text visible within the decision list at 1440 and at 390. Could break: the list's height on a phone; a long letter needs a clamp and a reveal.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the irreversible send is decided with its content in view
Before: 0 of 1 send decisions on the seed show the letter in the decision list
After: unmeasured - depends on where and how much of the letter is shown
Method: simulation - layout and density are a design call that needs a rendered window; nothing in the runner can see it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/Decide.tsx  send_reminder row: question: `This reaches ${email ?? "the client"}. You cannot un-send it.`
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/Evidence.tsx:130-135  the draft body block, inside the card
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level2/l2-the-card-3.css:155-160  .ln-decide-layer fixed, z-index 70, over the card

title: tempHome's reaper can fire mid-file and aim later tests at the dev books
body:
## Summary
`test/tmp-home.ts` restores the working directory and closes the books in a root-level `after` hook; a test file that awaits at top level between `test()` calls lets that hook run early, and every later test then writes to `examples/ledgerbox/data/ledgerbox.sqlite`, the running dev server's database.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/test/tmp-home.ts:18-27` registers `after(...)` that closes `db()` and `process.chdir(start)`; `openDb` resolves the file from `process.cwd()/data` (`examples/demo-kit/src/db/index.ts:55`) and memoises per path, so the next `db()` opens the app's own file. Reproduced this round: `test/ledgerbox-lanes-ui.test.ts` (before 3460add) awaited imports between tests, eight runs wrote 95 activity rows into the live books (43 drafts, 15 applied credits, 37 refiles), since reversed and diffed clean against a fresh seed. 3460add guards that one file (a `books()` assertion); the other ledgerbox test files are safe only because they happen to await everything first. Fixed means the harness refuses it, not each file: tempHome marks the scratch path (e.g. an env var or a global the kit's openDb checks under test) and openDb throws on any other file while it is set, or the restore moves to process exit.

## Flow
- a test file: tempHome(); test(A); await import(X); test(B) that writes
- node:test finishes A while X loads, runs the root after hook: cwd back to the app, db closed
- B's db() opens examples/ledgerbox/data/ledgerbox.sqlite and writes to the dev server's books

## Expected impact
Anyone running the ledgerbox suite while the dev server is up (this run had one on port 3001) - their books stop matching the seed with no signal. Measured by the seeded control already used in 3460add (a 50 ms top-level await between two tests) run against every ledgerbox test file. Could break: a test that legitimately opens a second file.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no test can write to the app's own database
Before: 1 file guarded (3460add) of 7 ledgerbox test files using tempHome; the seeded 50 ms await sends the other files' later tests to the live file
After: predicted: 0 of 7 - openDb refuses any non-scratch path under test
Method: simulation - the mechanism was reproduced and repaired this round in its own file; the harness fix is in test/tmp-home.ts and demo-kit, outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/test/tmp-home.ts:18  after(async () => { (await import("../lib/db")).db().close(); process.chdir(start); ... })
examples/demo-kit/src/db/index.ts:55  return join(process.cwd(), "data", `${appId}.sqlite`);
reproduced: in the gate test, process.cwd() = C:\...\examples\ledgerbox; live activity max id 1 -> 96 over 8 runs; repaired (rows id>=2 reversed), diff vs fresh seed: 0 rows of this round's left
guard: 3460add books() asserts cwd and db().file under the scratch home
instrument: the seeded control from 3460add (a 50 ms top-level await between two tests) applied to each ledgerbox test file, with the live file's activity max id read before and after

title: An unsent draft's card says Still owed; the lanes and totals count it out
body:
## Summary
The L2 card of the seed's unsent draft LB-2026-0055 leads with its balance as "Still owed" and opens Decide next step, while the lanes, the totals and now every act leave a draft out as owed by nobody.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Card.tsx:59` `owed = mark.balanceCents > 0` and `card/Head.tsx:60` prints "Still owed" from it; `lib/lanes/index.ts` owedCents skips COUNTED_OUT (6e5479b), `summarize` does, and since a50f929/6ec117a/32ccf40 the server refuses draft, record and send on a draft. 409b393 made the list hold those rows back, but the head figure and the `actionable` gate in Card.tsx still treat the draft as a debt, so the card opens with "Still owed" and a list in which most rows say Blocked. Fixed means one predicate for owed (the books' COUNTED_OUT, which `card/read.ts` NOT_A_DEBT now mirrors) in the head's word, and a decision on what a draft's card offers (void it; nothing else).

## Flow
- L0 -> Unfiled lane -> LB-2026-0055 (state draft)
- head: "$73,100 Still owed"; Decide next step offered
- the lane figure above it and the mast's totals do not count it

## Expected impact
A reader of the draft's card is told money is owed that the rest of the surface says is not. Measured by a parity test over the seed: the head's word vs the lane's owedCents for every mark. Could break: what the card offers for a draft (a design call on whether void stays).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one answer to 'is this owed' on the card and the sheet
Before: 1 of 1 seeded draft invoices: card says Still owed, lane and totals exclude it
After: predicted: 0 disagreements; the draft's card says it was never sent
Method: simulation - the figure is from the seed; the head is JSX and the card's offer for a draft is a wording and scope decision
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a parity test over buildSheet: for every mark, Card's owed predicate (moved to card/read.ts) equals !COUNTED_OUT && balance > 0, seeded red on LB-2026-0055

title: The send row offers a letter whose figures the books no longer hold
body:
## Summary
Since 32ccf40 `sendReminderAction` refuses a draft whose subject or body no longer matches the letter the books would write today (a part payment since the draft); `card/read.ts` actRefusal does not know that rule, so the list offers Send it and the press comes back as an error.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts` sendReminderAction compares the stored draft to `letterFor(invoice, draft.tone)` and fails "states figures the books no longer hold". `examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/read.ts` actRefusal("send_reminder") checks draft presence, not-a-debt, settled and disputed (409b393), not staleness. The parity test in `test/ledgerbox-lanes-ui.test.ts` passes only because the seed has no stale draft. Fixed means the sheet carries the fact (LnDetail.draft gets a `stale` flag computed by lib/lanes with the same composer, outside this context) and actRefusal blocks on it, with the parity test extended by a draft-then-credit case.

## Flow
- draft a reminder on an overdue invoice; apply a credit that part-pays it
- Decide next step: Send it is enabled
- Send it -> Send it: error toast "...states figures the books no longer hold..."

## Expected impact
The person is offered a press that can only fail, on the one act that reaches a client. Measured by the extended parity test (draft, credit, then compare the card's offer with the server's answer). Could break: nothing visible; one more Blocked line.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the list offers only what the books take
Before: on the seed 0 stale drafts; constructed case (draft then part-credit): the card offers, the books refuse (1 of 1)
After: predicted: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - the server rule is from the diff of 32ccf40; the stale fact must come from lib/lanes (ledgerbox-domain-lib's file), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts  sendReminderAction: const today = letterFor(invoice, draft.tone); if (today.subject !== draft.subject || today.body !== draft.body) return fail(...)
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/card/read.ts  actRefusal case "send_reminder": no staleness check
examples/ledgerbox/lib/lanes/index.ts  draft: draft ? { tone: draft.tone, body: draft.body } : null  (no stale flag)
instrument: extend the parity test in test/ledgerbox-lanes-ui.test.ts with draft -> matchAction part-credit -> compare actRefusal to sendReminderAction; needs a stale flag on LnDetail.draft from lib/lanes
